summary: Lewis County tower: wood tower 1911, steel tower 1919, closed end of 1970. Later pulled down, dates disputed. No tower on the mountain today.

facts.design: 47-foot steel Aermotor LS40 tower, erected 1919 over a 1911 wood tower
facts.status_note: No tower stands on the mountain today; the sources disagree on when and by whom it was pulled over.

access.note: Wikipedia says the public can visit the site; the land stays privately owned.

visit.trail_note: A forum visitor describes old logging roads and blackberry brambles on the mountain.

facts.agency: NYS Conservation Commission and Bureau of Forest Fire Control

events.note: Wood fire lookout tower built in May 1911 by the Conservation Commission
First observer on the payroll roster, Robert J. Kelly, from May 1911
47-foot steel tower bought in 1918 and erected in 1919, replacing the wood tower
Fire near Wolf Pond, Herkimer County, spotted from the tower by Warden Bruce Ferris on August 10, 1933; 25 men at the fire area by 1 p.m.
Last observer Alex J. St. Louis, through November 4, 1970
Closed at the end of the 1970 fire season; Wikipedia links this to aerial fire detection
Toppled by the State DEC and left, per the lookout history site; Wikipedia says the private owner pulled it over; a forum post says about 1975
State bought the development and recreation rights on the 18,000-acre tract; land and timber stayed private

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's lead says the steel tower was built in 1919. Its history section and the lookout history site say a wood tower went up in May 1911 and the steel tower replaced it in 1919. Both are true of different structures.

notes_for_editor: Built, staffing and the 1933 fire agree across sources (roster, lookout history site, Wikipedia). The fall of the tower is disputed and unresolved: closure end of 1970 (roster, Wikipedia); pulled over by the private owner per Wikipedia; around 1975 per a forum post quoting an unnamed source, which also says the toppled tower rests where it fell (the forum visitor could not recall tower pieces on the ground); State DEC toppling in 1984 per the lookout history site. Owner named Diamond International (Wikipedia) and Diamond Match Co. (forum); may be the same company under different names, not checked. Record coordinates are within roughly 40 m of the GNIS point Wikipedia gives. Do not confuse with the Rondaxe (Bald) Mountain tower near Old Forge. The Starr pictorial history PDF has a 1919 photo caption for this tower (credit Mrs. Nora Kuhl) but no image URL, so no photo was added. Forum evidence is secondhand and comes from a user forum. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 1933 date, the 1989 agreement, the observer names and the Old Forge/Rondaxe link were checked against the sources and added to the evidence.
